t: Palantir and Shopify Both Beat Earnings. Their Stocks are Falling Anyway.
desc: Apple, Palantir, Shopify, and several other major companies just reported earnings, and Wall Street is sending a clear message: Beating expectations isn't enough when profit margins are under pressure. In this video, Eric Bleeker, CFA, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., breaks down the biggest earnings movers and what their results reveal about the stock market. Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) beat revenue and earnings expectations as iPhone sales surged 17.5%, but disappointing gross margins raised concerns. Palantir (Nasdaq: PLTR) delivered explosive 96% revenue growth, yet investors are questioning slower growth in U.S. commercial contract value. Shopify (NYSE: SHOP) plunged 16% after missing revenue expectations and disappointing on free cash flow, despite beating earnings estimates. Elsewhere, Revvity (NYSE: RVTY) rallied 9% after raising guidance, while Fiserv (Nasdaq: FISV) jumped 10% on stronger earnings and expanded cost-cutting plans. Meanwhile, Zebra Technologies (Nasdaq: ZBRA) tumbled 16% despite beating estimates and raising its outlook, and Dynatrace (NYSE: DT) cut earnings guidance due to margin pressures. The big takeaway? Investors are increasingly focused on profitability, margins, and forward guidance rather than headline earnings beats alone.

Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) is up roughly 7%, and ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) is up 5%, helped by its control tower software that guides customers between models and agentic workloads. Anthropic is lagging, since Huang has pushed open-weight models that pressure leading labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. Bleeker's takeaway: if Huang keeps backing open weight model makers, Palantir, Cloudflare and ServiceNow, up 5% to 10%, should keep outperforming the 2% to 3% gains in the rest of software.
